findings.basis: Re-read of round 60, ruled in rule round 61, item 3. Read 76ac4b69f950 listed these 22 plain profiles, with google as the only recorded family. They hold 96 bundles where the true comes from Google's host entry and lands on SIMs whose own Google entry sets nothing: 204-04 (14), 204-08 (2), 206-01 (19), 206-20 (3), 208-09 (5), 208-10 (12), 208-15 (5), 208-20 (3), 214-05 (2), 214-07 (3), 216-01 (1), 216-70 (1), 222-01 (6), 222-10 (1), 232-10 (1), 242-01 (1), 242-02 (1), 260-06 (2), 293-70 (1), 310-300 (1), 311-588 (9) and 311-660 (3). A Pixel picks one entry per SIM, so only OCD's stack puts this true there. The first read's 'nothing changes' never looked at these bundles: the read acts only where the SIM's own entry says something else. 17 of the 96, sorted by entry name, are travel eSIMs. A read works per profile, so it cannot keep some of a profile's bundles. The bundles on 284-01, 284-03 and 284-05 are not here and stay on read 76ac4b69f950. 311-660: the plain word is old tmobile_us bundles (2022 to 2024). It does not come from the GID entries, and tmobileprivate_us is unset on every build read. Plain 311-660 SIMs do lose true on these 3 bundles, so the re-read's 'own SIMs lose nothing' does not hold for them. The Metro and Assurance GIDs keep true.
findings.effect: rtt_supported_bool (CarrierConfigManager.java:3418, default false at :12190). With true and ignore_rtt_mode_setting_bool at its default true (:11996), ImsManager.updateRttConfigValue provisions RTT on and keeps IMS turned on even when nothing else needs it (ImsManager.java:2756-2797, 1763-1785). ImsRegistrationTracker then adds TEXT beside each VOICE capability, using rtt_supported_while_roaming_bool when roaming (ImsRegistrationTracker.java:419-424, 585-598). AosHandleEmergencyMtc adds TEXT to the emergency registration whenever the key is true, with no roaming or network check (AosHandleEmergencyMtc.cpp:45-63). AosCondition.IsDeregRequiredForTty deregisters in TTY mode only when RTT is off, VoLTE TTY is off and the phone is combined-attached (AosCondition.cpp:998-1031). AosRegistration.UpdateNetworkFeatureRtt marks TEXT unavailable on a normal registration the network does not confirm (AosRegistration.cpp:1210-1245). A call type is cut down to the registered features (CallTypeUtil.cpp:24-66), and a voice call stays audio only (MtcMediaUtil.cpp:74-92, IdleState.cpp:550-552). Emergency TTY routing reads carrier_volte_tty_supported_bool, not this key (EmergencyCallDomainSelector.java:755-756, 1168-1169, 2045-2057). Telephony's own gate needs R.bool.config_support_rtt, which is false on 23.2 and on lineage-24.0 (config.xml:235, no overlay in the x1s device trees), so isRttSupported and isRttEnabled are false and the PhoneAccount has no RTT capability (PhoneInterfaceManager.java:7995-8035, TelecomAccountRegistry.java:1128-1154). Telecom still creates RTT streams for an emergency call when the calling app asks for RTT (CallsManager.java:2650-2662). ImsManager.java at android-17.0.0_r1 equals the tree. On a phone: admitted only for the most specific profile that sets the key, else the Google-lane value, else Android's default false (Serving.kt:405-440).
findings.risk: No harm was found. Served true, the emergency REGISTER gains TEXT with no network check, IMS stays on with VoLTE off and the native TTY deregistration stops. No source shows how these networks treat that tag from this stack, and no test can see it. The gain is small: the stock dialler cannot start RTT, since config_support_rtt is false. From holding, these SIMs follow Google's own entry both ways, and if Google sets true for an entry its SIMs get it with no read. A host's word does say how the host network treats the tag, which makes this the closest of the three parts, but a read cannot make that split. With RTT off and carrier_volte_tty_supported_bool false, a TTY user on a combined-attached SIM goes back to the native deregistration, as on any SIM with RTT off.

notes: Not admitted on this stack: the true on these 96 bundles is another entry's value, so the phone reads Android's default false. No harm was found, and nothing shows these networks lack RTT. The hold rests on missing basis, and it is no fact about the networks. Every SIM whose own Google entry sets true keeps it.
